paragraphs.source_en: Besides hunting mantises, I have also practiced the sport of catching cicadas. We commonly lump them together simply as cicadas, but in fact cicadas are not all one and the same thing. Just as among human beings there are oily rogues, obstinate fellows, and shabby wretches, so among cicadas there are aburazemi, minmin, and oshii-tsukutsuku. The aburazemi drones on and on, and is most disagreeable. The minmin cicada is overbearing too, and not at all lovable. Only the higurashi, the autumn cicada, is amusing to catch. This sort of cicada does not appear until summer is nearly over. When the autumn wind slips in under one's sleeve, brushes the skin, and makes one sneeze with a chill, then it begins to shake its tail-wings and cry without cease. It is such a persistent singer that, to my eye, its only appointed duties seem to be singing and getting caught by a cat. At the beginning of autumn, this is the fellow I make a point of catching. This is what I call the sport of cicada catching. Here I should explain to you all that, so long as they bear the name cicada, they will certainly not be lying on the ground. If one has fallen to the ground, ants are sure to gather round it. The ones I catch are certainly not those lying in territory already surrounded by ants. I catch the crowd perched high on tree branches, crying, 'oshii-tsukutsuku.' Since I am on the subject, I should like to ask learned men whether that cicada cries 'oshii-tsukutsuku' or 'tsukutsuku-oshii.' Depending on how the matter is interpreted, I think it may have no small bearing on the study of cicadas. It is precisely in such investigations that man surpasses the cat, and precisely here that man's pride resides; so if you cannot answer at once, you would do well to think it over carefully later. Of course, as far as my cicada-catching is concerned, it makes no difference whichever way it cries. I need only follow the sound up the tree and seize it firmly while the other party is crying in a frenzy. On the face of it this seems the simplest of sports, but in reality it is a highly laborious one. Since I possess four legs, I do not think I am especially inferior to other animals when it comes to walking on the earth. Judging, at least, by the mathematical knowledge of two legs versus four, I believe I do not lose to human beings. But when it comes to climbing trees, there are fellows considerably more skillful than I. Leaving aside the professional monkeys, even among human beings, the remote descendants of monkeys, there are some who must not be lightly dismissed. Climbing trees is, by nature, an unreasonable undertaking in defiance of gravity, so I do not regard inability to do it as any particular disgrace. Still, in the sport of catching cicadas, not being able to climb a tree causes no small inconvenience. Fortunately I have the useful weapon called claws, so I somehow manage to climb, though it is by no means as easy as it looks to bystanders. Nor is that the end of the problem, for cicadas can fly. Unlike Sir Mantis, once it has flown away, I may find myself in the sad position where all my tree-climbing has been no different from not climbing at all. The final difficulty is that I am sometimes in danger of being sprinkled all over with cicada urine.

paragraphs.source_zh: 除了捕螳螂之外，我也搞过捕蝉这类运动。一般我们只是简单地将它们称为蝉，其实，蝉不都是一样的东西。正像人类当中也有油滑蛋、顽冥儿、寒酸汉一样，在蝉中也有油蝉、暝暝蝉、寒蝉之分。油蝉叫起来没完没了，最讨厌。暝暝蝉很蛮横，也不招人喜欢。只有寒蝉捕捉起来最有趣。这种寒蝉不到夏末是不会出现的。每当秋风从腋窝侵入、吹拂着肌肤、寒意使人打喷嚏的时候，它才摇晃着尾翼开始鸣叫，而且叫个不停。在我看来，它除了鸣叫和供我捕捉之外，好像别无天职。在初秋，我就专捉这种家伙。这就是我的捕蝉运动。这里，我得向诸位说清楚，既然它们的名字叫蝉，那么它们是绝不会落到地面上来的。如掉落到地面上来，就会招来许多蚂蚁。我所捕捉的，决不是那些已经被蚂蚁包围躺在地面上的家伙。我专门捕捉停在高高的树枝上“呃唏吱——吱——”叫着的那些家伙。在这里，我要顺便向博学的人请教一下，这种蝉到底是“呃唏吱——吱——”地叫呢，还是“吱——吱——呃唏”地叫？我想由于解释的差异，这对于蝉的研究将会有重大的关系。人所以优于猫儿，也正是在研究这点上，人的自负也就是在这点上，所以若是马上回答不出来，那么最好请你们回头仔细考虑考虑。当然在我捉蝉这个问题中，随它怎样叫都是无关紧要的。我只要循声上树，利用它拼命狂叫的当儿，一把捉住它就是了。表面看来，这个运动似乎很简单，而实际上是个很劳累的运动。由于我有四条腿，所以我不认为自己在大地上行走会不如其他动物。我自以为根据两条腿与四条腿的数学概念来判断，我至少不会输给人类的。但是在爬树这点上，却有比我强者。那些以爬树为天赋本领的猴子姑且不论，就是在猴子的末裔的人类当中，也有一群不可轻侮的家伙。按理说，爬树是违背引力作用的一种逞能的事，因此即使不会爬，我也不认为是耻辱。然而在捕蝉运动上，如果不会爬树会带来许多不便。多亏我有爪子这个武器，总算勉勉强强可以爬上去，这事可绝不像旁观者想象的那样轻松。问题还不止于此，蝉是会飞的呀。它和螳螂君的情况不同，只要它一飞走，我就陷入爬与不爬没什么两样的悲惨境地。最后的问题是，我有时会遭到蝉尿撒一身的危险。
